Subject: Re: broken base(+derived) method calling mechanism -- Object won't search for Base (or derived) methods

Jim Cromie wrote: > You seem to be talking about a concrete case, > have you reduced it to a small program with ONE, TWO, THREE packages ? > If so, please attach it, it will clarify what youre asking, > and avoid issues of interpretation. ---- 	Aw...well, I have a fairly short program (at least with the Tk calls) and actually have two more classes "FOUR" and "main"... But each package (ONE, TWO, THREE and FOUR) have data items of the form ONE::field_one, TWO::field_two, THREE::field_three, FOUR::field_four. Each package (TWO-FOUR) is a parent of its predecessor (ONE-THREE). I have a key-handler in "THREE" that calls "field_one -> field_four" upon receipt of keys "1-4". The key-handler in THREE is called using a blessed reference that is (has isa relation) ONE, TWO, THREE, and FOUR... BUT once the key handler in THREE has been called, and even though it's package membership has been checked (isa ONE, isa TWO...), the subsequent call to methods for fields one, two and four are not found (not found "THREE::method"): The code:    my $active_key = index $single_key_commands, $key_event;    if ($active_key >= 0) {      $s->_check_package_names($key_event, $key_code);      $single_key_functions[$active_key]-> ($s, $key_event, $key_code);    } ... With keyboard input " 1234q" (space, keys 1-4 and q to quit) produces: --- key ' ', code 'space'    <=====space input $self isa ONE, isa TWO, isa THREE, isa FOUR, beep [1191631546.053390] main::beep key '1', code '1'        <====='1' $self isa ONE, isa TWO, isa THREE, isa FOUR, Tk::Error: Undefined subroutine &THREE::_field_one called at ./sht.pl line 223.      (command bound to event) key '2', code '2'        <====='2' $self isa ONE, isa TWO, isa THREE, isa FOUR, Tk::Error: Undefined subroutine &THREE::_field_two called at ./sht.pl line 223.      (command bound to event) key '3', code '3'        <====='3' $self isa ONE, isa TWO, isa THREE, isa FOUR, package THREE field three = 3 key '4', code '4'        <====='4' $self isa ONE, isa TWO, isa THREE, isa FOUR, Tk::Error: Undefined subroutine &THREE::_field_four called at ./sht.pl line 223.      (command bound to event) key 'q', code 'q'        <====='1' $self isa ONE, isa TWO, isa THREE, isa FOUR, _quiting... =================== Note that for keys 1,2,4 I get error messages saying that OO members above and below my current package (cur=THREE when key_handler called) are Undefined -- they aren't found in the other packages, even though "$self  isa ONE, isa TWO, isa THREE, isa FOUR," I.e. my blessed reference -- even though it has all the packages' blessings (packages ONE-FOUR) -- isn't searching the other classes'  "@ISA's". Somehow I'm guessing it is related to the "eval" in Tk being used to call the keyboard handler, BUT - that's why I wanted to know more about how perl actually implements the searching for parent classes in a call -- since the reference is properly blessed, but something else is missing to trigger perl not looking up the base (or in "FOUR"'s case, the "derived" class. This is a much smaller test case, but is still fairly large in order to include "derived, parent and grandparent classes" and the Tk-handling routines, but many of the lines are "form/dummy" lines needed to make 'strict and -w' happy (among other things). Hopefully the example code is reasonably str8forward.... I needed to install the following packages for this example:      Readonly, Tk, Tk::Image, Tk::JPEG, Image::Info plus the following debug/devel classes:      Data::Dumper, Devel::TraceSubs, Devel::XRay The bug occurs under 5.8.8 running on linux(Suseflavored), and Cygwin. Linda Note --
